acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: As New York City’s Democratic establishment attempts to resist the candidacy of Zohran Mamdani, we look back at another mayoral candidate who upset the established political machine.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
A history of the brief mayoral career of Harold Washington and its lessons for Black and white America, as told by people close to him.
Harold Washington died on November 25, 1987. This show was first broadcast ten years later, in 1997.
acts.title: Yesterday

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Ira revisits interviews with Chicago voters from the 1997 and 2007 rebroadcasts of this episode. In 1997, ten years after Harold Washington’s death, not much had changed in Chicago. By 2007, attitudes had begun to shift slowly, and another Black politician from Chicago was on the rise — Barack Obama. Ira also speaks to David Axelrod, an advisor to both Harold Washington and Barack Obama.
Listen to other versions of this act:
1997: The original broadcast. For years after Harold Washington's death, there were no Black mayors in any of the nation's largest cities. Ira explores why.
2007: Includes reporter Robert Wildeboer interviewing voters in wards that rejected Harold Washington in the 1980s.
2017: Includes Robert Wildeboer's interviews with those same voters, plus Barack Obama reading from his memoir about Chicago after Harold's death.

songs.a: sung by Harold Washington at his second inauguration

acts.title: The Present and the Future
